Catching Feebas: The Ultimate Guide/Evolving Feebas Via Beauty

Evolving Feebas into Milotic via Beauty

In games before the Prism Scale evolution method, Feebas evolves into Milotic after its Beauty condition reaches 170 and it levels up. Beauty is mostly invisible outside the contest condition screens, so planning your berries before feeding Feebas matters.

#0349

Feebas

#0350

Milotic

Checklist

Have Ready

  • ✓Feebas with Modest, Mild, Quiet, or Rash nature
  • ✓Stockpile of Dry berries: Pamtre, Hondew, Kelpsy, Cornn, or Wiki
  • ✓Game saved

Avoid

  • ✕Impish, Careful, or Adamant natured Feebas
  • ✕Saving after a failed attempt

Things to Know

  • Dry-flavor berries increase Beauty (when used as ingredients for Pokeblocks or Poffins).
  • A Pokemon can only eat so many Pokeblocks or Poffins before it refuses more. Ingredient quality matters because weak recipes can fill Feebas before Beauty reaches 170.
  • Prefer Modest, Mild, Quiet, Rash natures because they like Dry flavor. Avoid Impish, Careful, Adamant natures because they dislike Dry flavor.

Recommended Feeding Plan

Do not feed your Feebas incrementally. Stock up on berries, save the game, then make your Pokeblocks or Poffins and feed Feebas everything. Test whether it was enough by leveling up normally or using a Rare Candy. Do not save if Feebas refuses to eat more and does not evolve after leveling up. Reset, adjust your berry plan, and try again.

Berry Selection

The best berries for Beauty-focused Pokeblocks and Poffins are Pamtre Berry, Hondew Berry, Kelpsy Berry, Wiki Berry, Cornn Berry. Any berry with meaningful Dry flavor can contribute, but you should prioritize the strongest Dry berries you can reliably gather. The two Standouts in Emerald are Hondew and Kelpsy. as they have good availability and contribute significant dryness. Berry Location data for each game is available in each berry's item page.

Pamtre Berry

Baking only

Used for creating PokéBlocks and Poffins.

Hondew Berry

Effort drop

Drops Special Attack Effort Values by 10 and raises happiness.

Kelpsy Berry

Effort drop

Drops Attack Effort Values by 10 and raises happiness.

Wiki Berry

Picky healing

Held: Consumed at 1/2 max HP to restore 1/8 max HP. Confuses Pokémon that dislike dry flavor.

Cornn Berry

Baking only

Used for creating PokéBlocks and Poffins.

Game Notes

Ruby, Sapphire, and Emerald

The Lilycove City Contest Hall berry blender with three NPCs produces high-quality Pokeblocks, which helps raise Beauty efficiently before Feebas becomes full.

Hondew and Kelpsy are the most realistic options for a playthough. Pamtre is the strongest, but it is locked behind the Elite 4.

Diamond, Pearl, and Platinum

In Pokemon Platinum, Dry-Sweet Poffins can be bought downstairs in the Veilstone Department Store.

Fossil Pokemon Guide

Fossil items restore ancient Pokemon at fossil labs or restoration machines. This guide links each fossil item to its revived Pokemon, evolution details, and the curated fossil location notes on PokeLore. Open an individual fossil item page for curated game locations, revival levels, strengths and weaknesses.

Classic Fossils

Kanto Region Fossils

Helix Fossil

Restores Omanyte, Omastar.

Omanyte evolves into Omastar at level 40.

A bulky special attacker with strong Defense and useful Water/Rock coverage.

Dome Fossil

Restores Kabuto, Kabutops.

Kabuto evolves into Kabutops at level 40.

A physical attacker that becomes easier to use from Generation IV onward.

Hoenn Region Fossils

Root Fossil

Restores Lileep, Cradily.

Lileep evolves into Cradily at level 40.

A slow, durable Grass/Rock option built around survivability and recovery.

Claw Fossil

Restores Anorith, Armaldo.

Anorith evolves into Armaldo at level 40.

A more direct physical attacker with useful Bug and Rock damage.

Sinnoh Region Fossils

Skull Fossil

Restores Cranidos, Rampardos.

Cranidos evolves into Rampardos at level 30.

A simple, high-Attack fossil choice for teams that want immediate offense.

Armor Fossil

Restores Shieldon, Bastiodon.

Shieldon evolves into Bastiodon at level 30.

A defensive Rock/Steel wall with excellent bulk but low offensive pressure.

Unova Region Fossils

Cover Fossil

Restores Tirtouga, Carracosta.

Tirtouga evolves into Carracosta at level 37.

A bulky physical attacker that can become dangerous after Shell Smash.

Plume Fossil

Restores Archen, Archeops.

Archen evolves into Archeops at level 37.

A fast mixed attacker with excellent offenses but a limiting ability.

Kalos Region Fossils

Jaw Fossil

Restores Tyrunt, Tyrantrum.

Tyrunt evolves into Tyrantrum at level 39 during the daytime.

A straightforward physical Dragon/Rock attacker with strong biting moves.

Sail Fossil

Restores Amaura, Aurorus.

Amaura evolves into Aurorus at level 39 during the nighttime.

A slower special attacker with Ice coverage and several defensive weaknesses.

Standalone Fossils

Old Amber

Restores Aerodactyl.

Aerodactyl does not evolve, but can Mega Evolve in later generations.

A very fast Rock/Flying attacker that is often obtained late or after the main story.

Galar Fossils

Pokemon Sword and Shield use fossil halves instead of one complete fossil item. Combine two fossilized parts with Cara Liss on Route 6 to restore a Galar fossil Pokemon.

Fossilized Bird

Restores Dracozolt, Arctozolt.

Combines with Fossilized Drake for Dracozolt or Fossilized Dino for Arctozolt.

One half of two Galar fossil combinations in Pokemon Sword and Shield.

Fossilized Drake

Restores Dracozolt, Dracovish.

Combines with Fossilized Bird for Dracozolt or Fossilized Fish for Dracovish.

One half of the Dracozolt and Dracovish fossil combinations.

Fossilized Dino

Restores Arctozolt, Arctovish.

Combines with Fossilized Bird for Arctozolt or Fossilized Fish for Arctovish.

One half of the two Ice-type Galar fossil combinations.

Fossilized Fish

Restores Dracovish, Arctovish.

Combines with Fossilized Drake for Dracovish or Fossilized Dino for Arctovish.

One half of the Dracovish and Arctovish fossil combinations.

Herba Mystica Guide

Learn how Sweet, Salty, Sour, Bitter, and Spicy Herba Mystica work in Pokemon Scarlet and Violet, including story herbs, usable Bag items, raid farming, coach rewards, and sandwich uses.

Overview

Herba Mystica are rare sandwich ingredients in Pokemon Scarlet and Pokemon Violet. Usable Herba Mystica are especially valuable for high-level sandwich recipes and powers such as Sparkling Power, Encounter Power, Title Power, Humungo Power, Teensy Power, and Raid Power.

Sweet Herba Mystica

Used in recipes that specifically call for Sweet Herba Mystica.

Salty Herba Mystica

Commonly appears in many popular shiny-hunting sandwich recipe sets.

Sour Herba Mystica

Used in recipes that specifically call for Sour Herba Mystica.

Bitter Herba Mystica

Used in recipes that specifically call for Bitter Herba Mystica.

Spicy Herba Mystica

Used in recipes that specifically call for Spicy Herba Mystica.

Story Herbs vs. Usable Items

The Herba Mystica found during the Path of Legends Titan storyline are not added to your Bag as usable sandwich ingredients. Arven uses those story herbs immediately, and they restore Koraidon or Miraidon's travel abilities.

Sweet Herba Mystica

Titan: Klawf

Location: South Province Area Three

Salty Herba Mystica

Titan: Orthworm

Location: East Province Area Three

Sour Herba Mystica

Titan: Great Tusk or Iron Treads

Location: Asado Desert

Bitter Herba Mystica

Titan: Bombirdier

Location: West Province Area One

Spicy Herba Mystica

Titan: Dondozo and Tatsugiri

Location: Casseroya Lake

The story herbs restore Koraidon or Miraidon's abilities but do not become usable Bag items.

How to Unlock Usable Herba Mystica

Usable Herba Mystica are obtained mainly from eligible high-level Tera Raid Battles rather than from the Titan storyline. Five-star raids begin appearing after the ending credits. Six-star raids unlock after completing the Academy Ace Tournament and then completing 10 four-star or five-star Tera Raids. Seven-star raids are limited-time Poké Portal News events. Not every raid boss can drop Herba Mystica, and different bosses have different possible flavor rewards.

Tera Raid Sources

Usable Herba Mystica can be possible rewards from eligible 5-star raids, 6-star raids, and selected 7-star event raids. Seven-star raids are limited-time event raids delivered through Poké Portal News. Not every raid boss can drop Herba Mystica, and not every eligible raid boss can drop every flavor.

The important farming rule is to check the specific raid boss reward pool. This guide avoids duplicating a large boss-by-boss table until the site has a verified shared raid-drop dataset.

Other Sources

Hard-Difficulty Ogre Oustin'

In The Teal Mask, completing Hard difficulty Ogre Oustin' can award one of the five Herba Mystica as a recurring random reward. The flavor is not guaranteed, so treat this as a repeatable bonus farming route rather than a targeted flavor source.

League Club Room Coach Rewards

In The Indigo Disk, selected special coach interactions give finite Herba Mystica rewards. These are useful, but they are not repeatable farming sources.

  • Katy - three Sweet Herba Mystica
  • Tyme - three Bitter Herba Mystica
  • Larry - three Salty Herba Mystica
  • Saguaro - three Sour Herba Mystica
  • Kofu - three Spicy Herba Mystica

Flavor Comparison

Story Location: South Province Area Three

Usable Acquisition: Eligible high-star Tera Raid rewards, hard Ogre Oustin', and one finite League Club coach reward.

Common Sandwich Role: Used in recipes that specifically call for Sweet Herba Mystica.

Story Location: Asado Desert

Usable Acquisition: Eligible high-star Tera Raid rewards, hard Ogre Oustin', and one finite League Club coach reward.

Common Sandwich Role: Used in recipes that specifically call for Sour Herba Mystica.

Story Titan: Bombirdier

Story Location: West Province Area One

Usable Acquisition: Eligible high-star Tera Raid rewards, hard Ogre Oustin', and one finite League Club coach reward.

Spicy Herba Mystica

Story Titan: Dondozo and Tatsugiri

Usable Acquisition: Eligible high-star Tera Raid rewards, hard Ogre Oustin', and one finite League Club coach reward.

Common Sandwich Role: Used in recipes that specifically call for Spicy Herba Mystica.

Farming Tips

  • Focus on eligible high-star raids rather than the Titan storyline.
  • Check the raid boss reward pool before assuming a boss can drop Herba Mystica.
  • Use repeatable sources, especially eligible raids, for long-term farming.
  • Treat coach rewards as useful finite bonuses, not repeatable farming routes.
  • Save rare flavors for recipes that specifically call for them.
  • Separate broad sandwich farming advice from exact recipe requirements; different recipes may need different flavor combinations.

Frequently Asked Questions

Why did the Titan not give me usable Herba Mystica?

The Titan storyline herbs are story items. Arven uses them immediately, so they restore Koraidon or Miraidon's abilities but do not become Bag ingredients.

Can every 5-star raid drop Herba Mystica?

No. Herba Mystica rewards depend on the raid boss reward pool. Check the boss before assuming it can drop a herb.

Can every raid drop every flavor?

No. Different eligible raid bosses can have different possible Herba Mystica flavors.

Which flavor is best?

It depends on the recipe. Popular recipe sets may use different flavors, so match the Herba Mystica to the recipe you are making.

Are Herba Mystica repeatable?

Raid rewards and Hard difficulty Ogre Oustin' rewards are repeatable. Special coach rewards are finite.

Do I need DLC?

You do not need DLC for basic high-star Tera Raid farming, but Ogre Oustin' requires The Teal Mask and League Club coach rewards require The Indigo Disk.

What are Herba Mystica used for?

They are rare sandwich ingredients used in high-level recipes for powers such as Sparkling Power, Encounter Power, Title Power, Humungo Power, Teensy Power, and Raid Power.

Can story Herba Mystica be used in sandwiches?

No. Only the usable Bag items from sources such as eligible raids can be used as sandwich ingredients.

Raticate: Aquatic Pokemon?

One of the Pokemon with the most aquatic Pokedex entries is not a Water type, and it essentially learns no Water-type moves.

The First River Result

When you think of Pokemon that live around rivers, you probably picture Slowpoke, Marill, maybe Magikarp. But the first Pokemon that appears when you search the entire Pokedex for "river" is... Raticate?

Kanto RaticateAlolan Raticate

Multiple Pokedex entries talk about how it has webbed feet, swims, and even hunts for prey in the water.

Swimming in a river is one thing. Hunting prey in water is impressive. However, Pokemon Sun takes it even farther.

OCEANS. Not just streams or rivers. OCEANS.

This is well beyond the capabilities of something like a normal rat, and more like what you would expect from a marine mammal. That is why some fans speculate that Raticate's design may be based partly on a muskrat: its body is more compact than a typical rat, and its official lore keeps returning to water.

The Learnset Gap

Raticate is not just an overgrown sewer rat. It is apparently a semi-aquatic, ocean-crossing predator. So why can it not learn Surf, or basically any Water move for that matter? You can check Raticate's learnset against its entries and the mismatch stands out.

It learns Water Gun and Bubble Beam via TM in Gen I, but that can hardly be said to fit such an aquatic lifestyle.

Size Check

Perhaps it is too small to learn Surf? Certainly crossing an ocean on ones back would be a harrowing adventure. Raticate is listed at 2'4" tall. That is not huge, but it is still more than twice the listed height of Chewtle and Froakie, two much smaller Pokemon that can be used for surfing in the modern games.

Loading Raticate size chart...

How Game Freak Could Lean In

A Water/Normal typing would be one direct way to acknowledge the aquatic lifestyle, though it might feel a little like a different version of Bibarel. Another idea is a signature ability, maybe called River Rat, that makes Raticate's Normal-type moves super effective against Water-type Pokemon.

Raticate is not a fan favorite, and probably is not going to get very much love any time soon. It did get an Alolan form, so it may be waiting a while for another spotlight.
